q: Does the Fornalski et al. 2022 Monte Carlo tree, if reconstructed from the parent paper, actually produce the paper's headline numbers (82% full-repair, up to 7% two-dose AR effect, 0.126% global colony contribution, ~55x MC erosion of the analytical bound)?
basis: Every MC-derived headline number (Figs 2, 3-11, three of four Section 4 headlines) depends on the Fornalski 2022 Dose-Response simplified MC model, which is cited as ref [1] but has no public code release. The present paper does not tightly enough specify the per-time-step transition graph between {healthy, damaged, mutated, cancerous} states, nor the death/multiplication/classical-repair probabilities, to re-implement from Section 2 alone. This is the dominant blocker in the audit.
next_steps: Read Fornalski et al. 2022 Dose-Response (DOI 10.1177/15593258221103459) end-to-end plus the referenced Polish M.Sc./B.Sc. theses (refs [21,22,24,25]); implement the per-cell transition graph in NumPy/Numba (64,000 cells x 50 MC runs, T0=120 h); reproduce Fig 2 single-dose overlay and the 82% full-repair number first as the smallest self-contained MC test; if that lands within +/- 10% of the paper, extend to Figs 3-11 and the 0.126% global colony contribution. Budget: 3-5 solid days if the parent paper is well-specified, 1-2 weeks otherwise. Free endpoint: local CPU is sufficient (64,000 cells x 120 steps x 50 runs is O(10^8) operations, seconds per run).

q: Priming-dose window kinetics: does the exponential decay in delta-t implied by Eq (2)'s exp(-alpha_2 k) term with alpha_2 = 0.0832 h^-1 actually match the MC Fig 6 crossover claim that 'AR effect persists <= 80 h after the challenging dose'?
basis: The analytical exp(-alpha_2 * k) form gives 24 h -> peak, 48 h -> 13.5% of peak, 80 h -> 0.13% of peak. The paper's Fig 6 (MC scenario 4, delta-t = 100 h) shows the AR effect essentially vanishing, which is qualitatively consistent, but the specific crossover time (80 h) is a MC-ensemble property and cannot be tested from the analytical layer alone. It is also not clear whether the MC decays faster or slower than the analytical envelope, because the MC adds cell-death and multiplication dynamics on top of the P_AR window.
next_steps: Once the MC tree is reconstructed (Q1), sweep delta-t from 12 h to 240 h in 12 h steps at fixed (D_1=25 mGy, D_2=1500 mGy), record the AR-on vs AR-off survival delta, fit a decay time constant, and compare to alpha_2^-1 = 12.02 h from Eq (2). If the MC decay is substantially slower than the analytical envelope (i.e. cell division dilutes damaged cells before the AR window closes), that would be a novel finding not stated in the paper.

q: Is the paper's phenomenological P_AR(D,k) actually reducible to a specific molecular pathway (ATM/CHK2, p53/MDM2, NRF2/KEAP1, MRN complex kinetics), or is it fundamentally a fit-and-forget scalar that could equally describe several mutually incompatible mechanisms?
basis: The paper's title advertises 'mechanistic modelling', but the actual model is three empirical constants (alpha_0=22.9, alpha_1=79.4 mGy^-1, alpha_2=0.0832 h^-1) with no mapping to measurable pathway outputs (foci counts, protein phosphorylation, transcript levels). This is a common criticism of phenomenological AR models: any smooth peaked-in-D-and-k function fits the calibration data, so 'mechanism' claims are underdetermined.
next_steps: Take a published pathway-level AR model (e.g. Schollnberger et al. 2002 stochastic ATM/p53 model, or a more recent NRF2-based model), simulate its predictions at (D_1, delta_t) grid points, fit alpha_0/alpha_1/alpha_2 to those simulated outputs, and check identifiability: do multiple pathway-level parameter sets give the same (alpha_0, alpha_1, alpha_2)? If yes, Piotrowski et al.'s model is degenerate w.r.t. mechanism and the title claim is misleading. If no, then a fitted (alpha_0, alpha_1, alpha_2) is a pathway fingerprint and the paper is doing something stronger than its text admits.

q: Do the empirical constants (alpha_0, alpha_1, alpha_2, mu_0, mu_1) generalize across cell lines (V79, CHO, TK6, primary fibroblasts, tumor lines) and radiation qualities (protons, heavy ions, low-dose-rate gamma, high-LET), or are they specific to the human-lymphocyte X-ray calibration used in refs [21,22,25]?
basis: The paper uses two parameter sets (HBRA in-vivo and in-vitro human lymphocyte X-ray) and does not report cell-line or LET dependence. Adaptive response is known experimentally to vary by cell line by an order of magnitude and to weaken sharply above ~1 keV/um LET. If Piotrowski et al.'s constants are cell-line/LET-specific, the model's predictive scope is much narrower than the paper implies.
next_steps: Extract published dose-response curves for AR in V79 (Wolff 1996), CHO (Shadley & Wolff 1987), TK6 (Zhou et al. 2004), and primary human fibroblasts (Sasaki 2006); re-fit (alpha_0, alpha_1, alpha_2) per cell line; test whether the fitted constants cluster or spread. For LET dependence, use IMRT proton and 12C ion adaptive-response datasets (e.g. Belli et al. 2000). Report whether the paper's constants are outliers or representative. Free endpoint: scipy.optimize.curve_fit, ~1 hour per dataset.

q: The paper's Section 3.4 numerical inconsistency (P_C = 0.45 attributed to scenario 3, but Eq (5) at those parameters gives 0.155, and 0.45 only arises for scenario 2's parameters) -- is this a discussion-paragraph label swap, an Eq (5) coefficient typo, or a bullet-list parameter mistake, and does the resolution affect Figs 7-10 or just the text?
basis: Directly verified in claim C4c of this audit: Eq (5) with (mu_0=38, mu_1=11.5, d_dot=0.17) gives P_C=0.155, and (mu_0=882000, mu_1=1025, d_dot=0.002) gives P_C=0.454. The value 0.45 in Section 3.4's third paragraph is attributed to Fig 9 (scenario 3), but only scenario 2's parameters produce it. Three possible resolutions: (a) scenarios 2 and 3 are swapped in the discussion, (b) the bullet list has wrong parameters for scenario 3, (c) Eq (5) coefficients (11.5, 38) are typos. Each has different implications for whether the actual generated figures (7-10) show the right curves.
next_steps: Pixel-diff Figs 7 and 9 against re-generated Eq (5) curves under each of the three resolution hypotheses (e.g. plot P_C(d_dot) with in-vitro params, HBRA params, and each candidate typo-fix, then match the visual shape to the paper's Fig 9). If the paper's Fig 9 shape matches Eq (5) with in-vitro params (P_C = 0.155 peak), then the bullet list is right and only the discussion text is wrong. If Fig 9 shape matches Eq (5) with HBRA params (P_C = 0.454 peak), then the bullet list swapped scenarios 2 and 3. Once resolved, email K.W. Fornalski (corresponding author) with the finding; propose an erratum. Free tool: Python + pixel-diff of Figs 7-10 crops against synthesized P_C(d_dot) curves at the correct parameters.
